chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: The split between bebop and traditional players
summary: DeMichael asks about Charlie Parker and Dizzy. Hodes did not know them, but says the musicians who got press praise stopped playing with the traditional players.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Another unfortunate thing, I think, came out of that. And I felt that even in Louisville, Kentucky, because musicians were reading this all over the country. The schism that grew between the guys that wanted to play bebop and the guys that wanted to play traditional or whatever.
What was the relationship in New York between, say, yourself and Charlie Parker and Dizzy?

Well, I didn't know Charlie. And Dizzy came just after -- Dizzy and Charlie came in about 1947, and I didn't have anything to do with it then, didn't know them. But the other musicians that were getting plaudits, you didn't see them playing with us as much or anymore.
